newsitem.title: POLAND: KGHM GDRs boost Polish zloty vs basket, depos flat.
newsitem.headline: KGHM GDRs boost Polish zloty vs basket, depos flat.

text.p: The Polish zloty soared some 0.7 percentage point against the basket on Monday as foreign investors exchanged currencies to pay for the Global Depositary Receipts of the KGHM copper concern, dealers said.
They said the currency sales, which buoyed the zloty to its highest level in more than two weeks at 1.52/1.40 percent above the parity rate, totalled more than $100 million.
"It is difficult to be 100 percent sure, but the word on the market is that it is cash for the KGHM shares," said Tomasz Nowakowski of Bank Handlowy SA.

On Saturday the treasury set the strike price for the institutional and foreign tranches at 21 zloty per share. There are 35 million shares in the foreign tranche to be sold as GDRs through a consortium of foreign banks lead by Barclays de Zoette Wedd and Union Bank of Switzerland.
Analysts said the currency selling trend may spill over to Tuesday and even Wednesday.
"We might see more currency selling connected to the KGHM share payments until Wednesday," said Jaroslaw Laskowski, analyst at Pekao SA brokerage.
The zloty closed at 3.2640/85 to the dollar, up from 3.2950/55 on Friday and at 1.8695/15 to the mark, up from 1.8798/03.

On the money market O/N and T/N rates eased at bid but held flat at offer at 22.95/23.35 and 22.85/23.12 percent respectively. All minimum T-bill prices fell at the primary tender as demand totalled only 580 million zlotys against a 1.2 billion zloty offer.
"Falling T-bill prices and relatively high deposit offers are a result of pricing in expectations of a rate rise after last week's central bank's remarks," one dealer said.

Last Thursday the National Bank of Poland said the likelihood of a rate rise was growing because the bank may need to offset the increased domestic demand from a 1.9 percent budget gap planned for next year, instead of a balanced budget.
